authentication: A question is authenticated when its printed NTA question id is in the 24-05-2026 (First) final key for subject 306 and the key option id is one of its four printed option ids. Printed option ids are consecutive per question.
notes: Each question is printed in English, then Hindi; only the English is transcribed, read from the page images. Spelling and wording kept as printed (e.g. Q686 'nucelophilic', Q693 'Manganeses (II)', Q699 'ligetes', Q712 'strutcurally', Q680 'are true', Q691 'is same').
Page = the PDF page (pNN of the 50-page PDF; the printed footer 'Page N of 49' is one lower) where the question's English option ids were read.

Match tables are written as rows 'List-I item | List-II item' in the order the paper prints them. Structures and reaction schemes are described in square brackets (the paper prints them as drawings); formulas are written inline (superscript charges as ^, e.g. MnO4^-).
Q714: List-II prints drawings; (I) is the dicarboxylic acid (saccharic acid), (II) tryptophan, (III) gluconic acid, (IV) fructose. NTA's key gives option 4, which fits those drawings.

Q709: option 1 prints 'H3PO4 , H2O' in step (ii) (the NCERT reagent for replacing the diazonium group by H is hypophosphorous acid, H3PO2); NTA's key gives option 1 and it is the only diazotise-reduce-oxidise sequence offered. Kept as printed and flagged for the coverage stage.

Q701: (C) is printed '[Co(F6)]3-' and (D) '[Co(C2O4)]3-' (no subscript 3 on the oxalate); kept as printed. NTA's key gives option 1 (A, B, D, C), which matches the spectrochemical series for the intended [Co(C2O4)3]3-.
Q723: no reagent is printed over the arrow (phenol to salicylaldehyde); NTA's key gives option 2 (the ortho-CHCl2 sodium phenoxide intermediate of the Reimer-Tiemann reaction).
Q695: NTA's key gives option 3 ((A) and (D) only); NCERT gives the Cr-O-Cr angle in the dichromate ion as 126 degrees and says dichromate is used to prepare many azo compounds.

Q682, Q709 and Q711: OCR missed their English header lines, so their question ids and option ids were read from the page images (p8, p31, p33) and cross-checked with the Hindi copies; they then authenticated like the rest.
Every other key was read against NCERT and fits the English text as transcribed.

The shift's key has 50 rows, all single-answer, none dropped. NTA's final key for subject 306 holds 26 shifts; this paper is the 24-05-2026 First shift and all 50 question ids fall in that one shift (the two comprehension parent ids 226895790088 and 226895790094 are not key rows).

P1-226895790088.title: Electrochemical cells
P1-226895790088.text:
Electrochemical cells

We can construct innumerable number of galvanic cells on the pattern of Daniell cell by taking combinations of different half-cells. Each half-cell consists of a metallic electrode dipped into an electrolyte. The two half-cells are connected by a metallic wire through a voltmeter and a switch externally. The electrolytes of the two half-cells are connected internally through a salt bridge. Sometimes, both the electrodes dip in the same electrolyte solution and in such cases we do not require a salt bridge.

For the cell
Ni(s) | Ni2+(aq) || Ag+(aq) | Ag
The cell reaction is Ni(s) + 2Ag+ (aq) → Ni2+(aq) + 2Ag(s).

Nernst equation relates the emf of the cell with standard emf and the concentration of reduced and oxidized species.

P2-226895790094.title: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
P2-226895790094.text:
Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

Alcohols and phenols are formed when a hydrogen atom in a hydrocarbon, aliphatic and aromatic respectively, is replaced by –OH group. These classes of compounds find wide applications in industry as well as in day-to-day life. For instance, have you ever noticed that ordinary spirit used for polishing wooden furniture is chiefly a compound containing hydroxyl group, ethanol. The sugar we eat, the cotton used for fabrics, the paper we use for writing, are all made up of compounds containing –OH groups. The common name of an alcohol is derived from the common name of the alkyl group and adding the word alcohol to it. For example, CH3OH is methyl alcohol. The simplest hydroxy derivative of benzene is phenol. It is its common name and also an accepted IUPAC name. As structure of phenol involves a benzene ring, in its substituted compounds the terms ortho (1,2-disubstituted), meta (1,3-disubstituted) and para (1,4-disubstituted) are often used in the common names.

In ethers, the four electron pairs, i.e., the two bond pairs and two lone pairs of electrons on oxygen are arranged approximately in a tetrahedral arrangement. The bond angle is slightly greater than the tetrahedral angle due to the repulsive interaction between the two bulky (–R) groups.
